data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's mechanism collapses the distinction the problem asks for by invoking an infinite-time limit in which catastrophic shared-cause probability approaches 1. But the problem concerns whether a decentralized network is more resilient under finite, operational conditions and what evidence distinguishes independent from merely uncorrelated failures. SRC_002 provides no causal mechanism operating within a finite horizon; its 'in the limit of infinite time' argument is a limiting argument, not a mechanism. It also assumes the same catastrophic shock affects all nodes 'regardless of topology' without specifying the causal channel — air-gapped or offline nodes would not be affected by an internet backbone failure, a causal distinction its mechanism ignores. Thus it fails to engage the problem's demand for a discriminating causal mechanism.
